articles.title: How Australia’s tipping culture got awkward – and what to do about it
articles.summary: Ten per cent, 20%, 25%? If you’ve made a cashless payment at a cafe or pub lately there’s a reasonable chance you’ve been prompted to tip. Isabella Lee looks into the arrival of US-style tip requests and where that money really goes.
body: Alyx: You’ve been thinking about tipping for a few months now, and wrote about it this week. What first sparked your interest? Isabella: I came across a post in a bartenders’ Facebook group from someone asking if their experience of having tips withheld was normal. The comments shocked me! There were more than 30 responses, with the majority of them calling out venues where they’d also been denied their tips. It made me think, if this practice was so common, why hadn’t anything been done about it?

Alyx: When you did some more digging, what did you find out? Isabella: I reached out to Fair Work to ask what legislation there was around paying out tips to staff. They told me there is none. So the original poster hadn’t experienced wage theft because the employers weren’t actually breaking any rules. It’s not just management who can dip their hand in the tip jar. Cashless payment systems take a percentage from every transaction made too. It’s pretty cheeky that the systems that allow a business to ask for tips – which changes customers’ decision-making behaviour – also get a cut.
points: If you’ve made a cashless payment at a cafe or pub lately there’s a reasonable chance you’ve been prompted to tip.

articles.title: The moment I knew: For Valentine’s Day he gave me a heart covered in fake blood. I was appalled – and thrilled
articles.summary: Will Huxley thought Garrett looked like a Heathcliff type. They bonded over their shared love of Kate Bush. Then one day Garrett handed over an ornate gift box. Find more stories from the moment I knew series.
body: I n 2006 I’d just graduated film school at the Victorian College of the Arts and was working at the ABC in Melbourne. It was a pretty tumultuous time of my life. I had just broken up with my best friend and high school sweetheart – whom I adored – and was in the process of coming out.

I was drinking too much and in breaks from the chaos I’d find myself drawn to the local video store. That’s where I first saw Garrett behind the counter. I had an instant crush on him and spent a lot of time perusing the art house section, so he would see how creative and cultured I was.
I never had the guts to talk to him but one night in spring we ran into each other at a party. We hit it off and arranged a date at a cafe in the city.

I was obsessed with Kate Bush and Wuthering Heights, and Garrett struck me as this sort of Heathcliff type; he was a dark, handsome artist with very dramatic, gothic vibes. That day we talked about art and the things that we love. I was so excited that he shared my passion for Kate Bush, and listening to Hounds of Love on repeat. We talked about John Waters and Cindy Sherman and all these artists that were really formative for us.
points: Will Huxley thought Garrett looked like a Heathcliff type.

articles.title: My week wearing ankle weights: 'I was helping kickstart my muscles'
articles.summary: When a knee injury forced me to change my fitness routine, I added Sportneer ankle weights – and got a decent workout. I’m a personal trainer. Here’s the equipment I use. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: M y exercise regimen has changed drastically over the last 15 years. A self-confessed cardio queen in my 20s and 30s, I alternated days at the gym with dance and Hiit classes and endured long bouts on the full complement of cardio equipment. And then my body caught up with me. First it was bursitis in my knee, which my doctor called “burpee-itis” from the ridiculous amount of the exercises I was performing. “You have to listen to your body,” he lightly chided as he poked at my swollen kneecap. Once my lower back started to complain, I had to start making serious concessions.

Thankfully, finding new ways to stay in shape was not as hard as I thought. A quick pivot led me to strength training, barre and pilates classes, and lots and lots of walking. My knee was still keeping me from doing a ton of basic leg work including squats and lunges, so ankle weights seemed like an easy solution. After doing some research on what would fit my specific needs, I decided on Sportneer ankle weights and used them daily for a week to see if they could enhance my lower body workouts.

articles.title: The power of AI is worrying senior Labour figures – as is the fear of ‘falling behind the public’
articles.summary: Westminster appears to be waking up to warnings over AI safety, with concerns over its use by extremist groups and bad actors. “I have this sense that, within a few months, AI is going to be all anyone is talking about,” said one cabinet minister, with an ominous stare.
body: It was Labour conference, with everyone from ministers to activists jubilant at Andy Burnham’s takeover and a bounce in the polls after the change of leader.
But a number of senior Labour figures were privately starting to name the power of AI as the thing worrying them most, alongside the immediate pressures on the cost of living and fragile economy.

One cabinet minister – with a brief unrelated to technology – told the Guardian that dangerous, out-of-control AI was the issue keeping them up at night, fretting about the threat to humanity. It was “not killer robots” causing the worry, they explained, but the idea of a huge amount of concentrated, super-intelligent power potentially ending up in the hands of bad actors.
Another expressed concern that the government was “falling behind the public” in terms of dealing with worries about AI safety – and that it needed to catch up fast.
points: Westminster appears to be waking up to warnings over AI safety, with concerns over its use by extremist groups and bad actors.

articles.title: Île Seguin: This tiny island just outside Paris is about to become the city's newest cultural destination
articles.summary: A sleek new contemporary art center is opening on Île Seguin this October, marking another milestone in the transformation of this former industrial site on the Seine.
body: Paris is hardly short of museums and is a real paradise for art lovers. Not only could you spend weeks hopping between its biggest hitters—namely the Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, and Musée de l'Orangerie —but the city also has an incredible collection of smaller museums and galleries that are less frequented by tourists, yet definitely deserve some love. If, like me, you have a particular soft spot for contemporary art, Gagosian and Perrotin are just two of the many galleries worth visiting in the city, and they're among my favorites to browse on a rainy Parisian day.

Although the city center has countless museums to visit, this autumn, one of the French capital's most exciting cultural openings is happening somewhere you might not immediately think to look: on a small island in the Seine just beyond the city limits.

Île Seguin sits at Boulogne-Billancourt, southwest of central Paris and around a 10-minute walk from the end of Métro line 9. Once synonymous with industry—Renault operated its enormous factory here for much of the 20th century—the island has been gradually reinventing itself as a cultural district. Now, the next major piece of the puzzle is about to be added.
points: A sleek new contemporary art center is opening on Île Seguin this October, marking another milestone in the transformation of this former industrial site on the Seine.

articles.title: My Favorite Airbnb: A Hudson Valley Retreat With a Creekside Hot Tub and Sauna
articles.summary: Between its storybook interiors and proximity to small-town shops, farm stands, & cider orchards, this Hudson Valley stay is one of my top upstate discoveries.
body: Getting 12 people to agree on a weekend away is an exercise in logistics. Someone wants to hike; someone else would rather browse antique shops; a few people are already asking what’s for dinner. My ideal group getaway? One that leaves room for all of it, with a house you're excited to return to in between excursions. On a recent October weekend, my friends and I—a total of six couples—found that combination at Schoonmaker Retreat, tucked in the quaint Hudson Valley hamlet of High Falls.

As a lifelong New Yorker, I’ve made plenty of trips to the Catskills and Hudson Valley, but High Falls, Rosendale, and Accord were towns I hadn’t yet gotten to know. Rosendale had been on my radar thanks to the introduction of Six Bells Countryside Inn, a delightfully whimsical, British-inspired hotel, and the surrounding area seemed ripe for a fall weekend of vintage shopping, cider tasting, and lots of leaf-peeping. We lucked into a real Goldilocks window, with timing just right for trees to stand ablaze with reds, yellows, and the last bits of green. The weather was crisp, but still sunny enough to sit outside for hours, from long orchard lunches to cozy s’more nights.
points: Between its storybook interiors and proximity to small-town shops, farm stands, & cider orchards, this Hudson Valley stay is one of my top upstate discoveries.

articles.title: The 25 Best Airbnbs in Italy, From Puglia to the Dolomites
articles.summary: Whether you’re dreaming of rugged coastlines or rambling hillsides, these are the best Airbnbs to book in Italy, from Puglia to Tuscany to the Amalfi Coast.
body: There is always a reason to talk about Italy. Perhaps it’s to celebrate the country’s craft heritage, which has been passed down for generations. Or to explore the merits of its multitudinous pasta shapes and grape varietals (around 500 each, if you can believe). The natural landscapes are so mind-bogglingly beautiful they tend to invite clichés, and the country’s landmarks—from Rome’s Colosseum to Florence’s Ponte Vecchio—manage to awe and inspire even the most jaded travelers among us. Suffice it to say, it is always a good time to visit Italy.

If you’re itching to plan a dolce vita getaway, start by perusing the compelling vacation rentals below to pick out a home base. We’ve scoured listings in the country’s most breathtaking regions—from a Sardinian home with a sea access staircase built into the rocks, to a 1700s-era apartment nestled in the old Sicilian town of Modica. Or perhaps you’re in need of isolation? We found a home in a car-free, medieval village in the hills of Tuscany. Whatever your pursuit, the 25 Airbnbs below deliver in spades.
